name: Blister card of narrow-spectrum antibiotics
description: Mild antibiotic tablets. Helps the body fight off an infection for twelve hours but rarely cures one alone.
notes: Plain white tablets and a green band set it apart from batch 8's red and yellow broad-spectrum capsules. Infection resistance has no content field yet.

name: Bag of cannabis
description: Dried cannabis buds in a zip bag. Smoked to ease nausea and pain and lift the mood. Habit-forming.
notes: plastic-clear draws the bag; it stays see-through in the game, so the olive buds inside show there, though the look tiles draw the bag opaque. Nausea, appetite, mood and habit have no content fields yet.

name: Jar of wintergreen ointment
description: A jar of ointment smelling of wintergreen. Rubbed into a wound, it dulls the pain and keeps it a little cleaner.
notes: An ointment, so the item is the whole 50 ml jar, as with the existing antiseptic, and the row carries 60 g with the jar against the reference's 40 g. The reference's 250 ml volume does not fit 40 g of ointment, so the jar follows the mass; the look step allows this as a per-unit reference. Pain relief and mild antisepsis should follow the existing antiseptic's fields when the refactor applies drafts.

name: Vial of fast-acting sedatives
description: Strong anti-anxiety tablets. Calms quickly and brings on sleep, but blurs memory and is badly addictive.
notes: The id describes the drug instead of the reference's brand. A white cap sets the vial apart from batch 8's blue-capped painkillers. plastic-amber draws the vial; it stays see-through in the game. Sedation, memory loss and addiction have no content fields yet.

name: First aid case
description: An empty red plastic case with a white cross and a carry handle. Holds bandages and medicine.
notes: The empty case, which carries the reference's 200 g; its contents are separate items. The container follows the existing ammo can's fields; the pocket grid is a placeholder for the 2.9 L the reference gives.

name: Plastic barrel
description: A blue 30 gallon plastic barrel with screw bungs in the top. Holds water or fuel without leaking.
notes: Closed-head with two bungs, the common blue drum, so it reads apart from the two steel drums. The reference's 'watertight lid' becomes the bungs. Liquid storage of about 115 L has no content field yet; the size is a placeholder for a thing too big to pocket. The aluminium tank variant rides on this model as the reference groups it.

name: Steel drum (100 L)
description: A red 30 gallon steel drum with a lid held by a bolted clamp ring. Holds liquids and stands over a fire.
notes: Open-head with a clamp ring, so it reads apart from the closed 200 L drum. The reference's 7.6 kg is kept though a real 30 gallon steel drum weighs nearer 14 kg; its box is 1.7 times the reference volume because the reference gives the contents, not the drum. cooking stands for the reference's boiling quality; liquid storage has no content field yet, and the size is a placeholder. The 200 L aluminium tank is a variant here as the reference groups it, though it would fit steel_drum_200's size better; the fire barrel rides here too.

name: Steel drum (200 L)
description: An olive 55 gallon steel drum with two screw bungs in the top. Holds fuel or water and stands over a fire.
notes: Closed-head with two bungs. Its box is 1.5 times the reference volume because the reference gives the contents, not the drum. cooking stands for the reference's boiling quality; liquid storage has no content field yet, and the size is a placeholder. The variants ride on this model as the reference groups them, though the 30 gallon barrel would fit plastic_barrel better and the oil extractor would want its own still parts.
